correctness.rationale: The fixed-content binary-word bijection gives a uniform positive composition conditional on R. Exact singleton-count coefficients follow by choosing singleton positions and distributing excess units. The ratio for consecutive run counts is increasing in S on overlapping supports, with support endpoints moving right; thus every two-by-two joint minor is nonnegative, including zeros. Vandermonde factorial moments yield the stated rational covariance. Independent enumeration and rational checker verified 2,304,064 exact finite assertions; the infinite result rests on the symbolic proof, not that enumeration.

originality.rationale: A targeted published-finding corpus search, accessible own-claim comparison, and primary literature checks found classical marginal run enumeration and general composition part-count theory, but no directly covering finite-sample singleton-count likelihood-ratio/TP2 statement. The new argument supplies an explicit adjacent-row ratio and full joint dependence conclusion. Coverage by inaccessible older multivariate runs literature remains a declared historical-priority risk; the finding does not claim unique discovery of the enumeration formula.
residual_risks: Some 1939–1994 classical run-length literature was reachable only via bibliographic citations or abstracts; an implicit or explicit equivalent conditional order may exist there.
A general multivariate composition enumeration, if it already proves total positivity or includes a recognized ordering theorem, could dominate this result; the consulted texts did not show that.
The run-count and composition formulas themselves are classical and are not claimed new.

value.rationale: For fixed-content runs tests, total one-run count and number of isolated successes measure distinct aspects of clustering. TP2 yields simultaneous ordering of every singleton-count upper tail and monotone conditional likelihood ratios, a stronger, structurally useful comparison than known mean or one-run marginal calculations. The exact positive covariance provides a finite-sample scale and allows properly calibrated joint dependence interpretation without independence approximations; this is a natural statistic and an all-parameter theorem, not a selected numerical window.
